meta.title: Husonym — Data anonymization and synthetic data
meta.description: Husonym anonymizes your production databases, generates synthetic data that matches your schema, and carves out a consistent subset — without breaking referential integrity.
meta.ogTitle: Husonym — Production data, without the personal data
meta.ogDescription: Anonymize production, generate synthetic data and subset your databases — so dev, CI and staging run on realistic data with no legal exposure.
meta.ogImageAlt: Husonym — data anonymization and synthetic data orchestration

hero.lede: Husonym anonymizes your databases, generates synthetic data that matches your schema, and carves out a referentially intact subset — so dev, CI and staging finally run on realistic data, with no legal exposure.
hero.note: A walkthrough on your own tables, with no commitment.
hero.cardFoot: 44 built-in transformers, or your own in JavaScript

problem.titleHtml:
Copying prod is a liability.
Hand-written fixtures are useless.
problem.body: A production dump in a dev environment is personal data on the loose, duplicated into backups nobody owns any more. Hand-written fixtures are three rows per table: they reproduce no real bug and rot the moment the schema changes.

steps.title: Four steps, once. After that it's a job.
steps.step1Body: One source, one or many destinations: Postgres, MySQL, SQL Server, MongoDB, DynamoDB, S3, Cloud Storage.
steps.step2Body: Husonym reads your schema and proposes a transformer per column. You adjust, you preview.
steps.step3Body: One SQL filter per table. Husonym walks the foreign keys and hands you a consistent dataset.
steps.step4Body: The job runs on Temporal: retries, replay, scheduling — and the same job called from your CI.

anonymization.title: Masking is decided column by column.
anonymization.body: Forty-four built-in transformers cover the common types: email, E164 phone, name, address, SSN, card number, UUID, timestamp. Every column keeps its format, its length and its uniqueness — your NOT NULL and UNIQUE constraints still hold.
anonymization.list1: Schema detection, with a transformer proposed on each column
anonymization.list2: Preview the result before anything is written
anonymization.list3: Passthrough, Null or column default for everything that isn't sensitive
anonymization.visualFoot: Format is preserved: constraints and application-side validation keep passing.

synthetic.title: No data? Generate it.
synthetic.body: Husonym fills an empty database from the schema alone. And for the fields that need to mean something — a product label, a reason for a visit, a customer comment — plug in OpenAI, Anthropic or TogetherAI with your own prompt.
synthetic.list1: Generation from scratch, with no seed data at all
synthetic.list2: LLM transformers with a custom prompt, per column
synthetic.list3: Pick the volume: as many rows as your test actually needs
synthetic.prompt: A realistic support ticket subject for an online billing service, in English, 60 characters maximum.
synthetic.row1: Cannot find my March invoice in the customer portal
synthetic.row2: I was charged twice for this month's subscription
synthetic.row3: How do I change the bank account on my plan?
synthetic.visualFoot: No real data reaches the prompt: the model only ever sees your instruction.

subsetting.title: 104 GB in production. 1.2 GB on your laptop. The same joins.
subsetting.body: One WHERE per table, and Husonym handles the rest: it walks the foreign keys so the subset stays joinable. Self-referencing tables and circular dependencies are supported, as soon as a nullable column in the cycle gives it an entry point.
subsetting.list1: One SQL filter per table, written in your database's own dialect
subsetting.list2: Related tables pulled in automatically by following foreign keys

orchestration.title: A job, not a script somebody re-runs by hand.
orchestration.body: The engine is Temporal. An interrupted job resumes where it stopped, a run replays identically because the pipeline is event-sourced, and every execution leaves its logs behind. Job hooks fire whatever SQL you want before and after the sync.
orchestration.list1: Failure recovery and a retry policy per activity
orchestration.list2: Cron scheduling, plus triggering from the CLI or the API

customCode.title: When no transformer fits, you write your own.
customCode.body: A JavaScript transformer receives the cell value and the whole row, and returns whatever you need. Enough to honour a business format, derive a value from another column, or hold a consistency Husonym cannot guess at.
customCode.list1: Access to the full row, not just the cell
customCode.list2: Reusable across columns and across jobs
customCode.list3: Versioned alongside the rest of your configuration

gitops.title: Your datasets are code.
gitops.body: A Terraform provider describes connections, mappings and jobs next to the rest of your infrastructure. The CLI triggers the job from a pipeline, seeding the CI database before the end-to-end suite runs.
gitops.list1: Terraform provider for connections, jobs and mappings
gitops.list2: CLI and API keys for non-interactive pipelines
gitops.list3: Every configuration change reviewed in a pull request

connectors.body: Sources and destinations supported today. Missing one from your stack? Let's talk — we add connectors.
connectors.footnote: This list grows with every release. Tell us which database you run.

trust.title: Your data never leaves your perimeter.
trust.body: The engine reads your source and writes your destination without a copy going anywhere else. No sample is shipped to a third-party service for analysis — unless you wire up a model provider yourself, and you then decide exactly which columns reach it.
trust.card1Body: Credentials encrypted at rest, bastion access for databases that aren't publicly reachable, and a dedicated service account rather than your admin credentials.
trust.card2Body: A properly anonymized database takes your dev and staging environments out of GDPR, HIPAA, FERPA and DPDP scope.
trust.card3Body: Roles per account, logs kept for every execution, an event-sourced pipeline: every run is replayable and auditable.
trust.card4Body: We recommend restoring a snapshot to a dedicated database on a schedule and pointing Husonym at that. Less load on prod, less exposed surface.
trust.disclaimer: Husonym is a tool: whether your processing legally qualifies as anonymized remains your call.

sovereignty.title: Your data stays yours.
sovereignty.body: Husonym works on your data where it already lives. Nothing is copied to an intermediate platform, nothing is retained once the job finishes, and every execution leaves an auditable record of what was read, transformed and written.
sovereignty.note: How it is put in place adapts to your infrastructure and compliance constraints. It is the first thing we go through in a demo.
